newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Nov industrial output falls 5.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Nov industrial output falls 5.2 percent.

text.p: Singapore's manufacturing output fell 5.2 percent year-on-year in November due to reduced production of electronics and transport equipment, the Economic Development Board said on Friday.
Analysts said the fall was not unexpected given the sharp 8.8 percent fall in November non-oil domestic exports announced by the Trade Development Board last month.
The EDB said output of electronic products declined 9.0 percent in November over the same period last year.

"The industry was weighed down by decreases in most major segments like personal computers, other computer peripherals, semiconductors, consumer electronics and telecommunication equipment even though output of disk drives and printed circuit board assemblies went up in response to higher demand," the EDB said.
Cumulative electronics output for the first 11 months of 1996 grew 7.4 percent.
The output of transport equipment fell 6.4 percent in November.
"Despite the increase in the aviation segment, the shrinkage in the marine segment pulled down the overall industry performance," the EDB said.
Cumulative output for the transport industry fell 8.1 percent in the first 11 months.
The chemical industries -- including petroleum, petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and specialised chemical industries -- grew 16.9 percent in November.
EDB said the increase came from the petrochemical and pharmaceutical industries.
November's output of petroleum products was maintained at about last year's level, leading to a cumulative output growth of 5.3 percent for the first 11 months.
